passages.text: These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah: In the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa, Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived with men from Judah. So I questioned them about the remnant of the Jews who had survived the exile, and also about Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the son of Hacaliah.
He spoke these words.
It was the month of Chislev.
It was the twentieth year.
I was in the citadel of Susa.
Hanani came to me.
Hanani was one of my brothers.
He brought men from Judah.
I asked them about the Jews who survived the exile.
I also asked them about Jerusalem.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֥י נְחֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן־ חֲכַלְיָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י בְחֹֽדֶשׁ־ כִּסְלֵו שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃ וַיָּבֹ֨א חֲנָ֜נִי אֶחָ֧ד מֵאַחַ֛י ה֥וּא וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁאָלֵ֞ם עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֧ים הַפְּלֵיטָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־ נִשְׁאֲר֥וּ מִן־ הַשֶּׁ֖בִי וְעַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And they told me, “The remnant who survived the exile are there in the province, in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah is the son of Hacaliah.
He was in the citadel of Susa.
Hanani, his brother, and men from Judah came to him.
Nehemiah asked them about the Jews who survived the exile.
He also asked about Jerusalem.
They answered him.
They said some Jews survived the exile.
These Jews are in the province.
They are in great trouble.
They are in disgrace.
The wall of Jerusalem is broken down.
The gates of Jerusalem are burned with fire.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לִי֒ הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִ֞ים אֲשֶֽׁר־ נִשְׁאֲר֤וּ מִן־ הַשְּׁבִי֙ שָׁ֣ם בַּמְּדִינָ֔ה בְּרָעָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה וּבְחֶרְפָּ֑ה וְחוֹמַ֤ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ מְפֹרָ֔צֶת וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ נִצְּת֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the son of Hacaliah.
He lived in the citadel of Susa.
He heard troubling news about Jerusalem and the Jews who survived exile.
When Nehemiah heard these words, he sat down.
He wept.
He mourned for many days.
He fasted.
He prayed before the God of heaven.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כְּשָׁמְעִ֣י׀ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה יָשַׁ֙בְתִּי֙ וָֽאֶבְכֶּ֔ה וָאֶתְאַבְּלָ֖ה יָמִ֑ים וָֽאֱהִ֥י צָם֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Then I said: “O LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion with those who love Him and keep His commandments, let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to hear the prayer that I, Your servant, now pray before You day and night for Your servants, the Israelites. I confess the sins that we Israelites have committed against You. Both I and my father’s house have sinned.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah spoke to God.
God is the LORD.
God is the God of heaven.
God is great.
God is awesome.
God keeps His covenant.
God shows loving devotion to those who love Him.
God shows loving devotion to those who keep His commandments.
Nehemiah asked God to listen.
Nehemiah asked God to see.
Nehemiah asked God to hear his prayer.
Nehemiah prayed day and night.
Nehemiah prayed for the Israelites.
The Israelites are God’s servants.
Nehemiah confessed the sins of the Israelites.
Nehemiah said the Israelites sinned against God.
Nehemiah said he sinned.
Nehemiah said his father’s house sinned.
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֗ר אָֽנָּ֤א יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם הָאֵ֥ל הַגָּד֖וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָ֑א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וָחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃ תְּהִ֣י נָ֣א אָזְנְךָֽ־ קַשֶּׁ֣בֶת וְֽעֵינֶ֪יךָ פְתֻוּח֟וֹת לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֶל־ תְּפִלַּ֣ת עַבְדְּךָ֡ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִי֩ מִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל לְפָנֶ֤יךָ הַיּוֹם֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה עַל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ וּמִתְוַדֶּ֗ה עַל־ חַטֹּ֤אות בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֣אנוּ לָ֔ךְ וַאֲנִ֥י וּבֵית־ אָבִ֖י חָטָֽאנוּ׃

passages.text: We have behaved corruptly against You and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that You gave Your servant Moses.
passages.sermon:
We have acted corruptly against You.
We did not keep Your commandments.
We did not keep Your statutes.
We did not keep Your ordinances.
You gave these commandments, statutes, and ordinances to Moses, Your servant.
passages.original: חֲבֹ֖ל חָבַ֣לְנוּ לָ֑ךְ וְלֹא־ שָׁמַ֣רְנוּ אֶת־ הַמִּצְוֺ֗ת וְאֶת־ הַֽחֻקִּים֙ וְאֶת־ הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתָ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Moses when You said, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations, but if you return to Me and keep and practice My commandments, then even if your exiles have been banished to the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for My Name.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses, His servant.
God gave Moses a command and a warning.
God said, “If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations.”
God also gave a promise.
God said, “If you return to Me, I will gather you again.”
God said, “If you keep My commandments and do them, I will bring you back.”
God said, “Even if your exiles are at the farthest edge of the heavens, I will gather them from there.”
God said, “I will bring them to the place I have chosen for My Name to dwell.”
passages.original: זְכָר־ נָא֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתָ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדְּךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַתֶּ֣ם תִּמְעָ֔לוּ אֲנִ֕י אָפִ֥יץ אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַמִּֽים׃ וְשַׁבְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ מִצְוֺתַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אִם־ יִהְיֶ֨ה נִֽדַּחֲכֶ֜ם בִּקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מִשָּׁ֣ם אֲקַבְּצֵ֔ם וַהֲבוֹאֹתִים אֶל־ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתִּי לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: They are Your servants and Your people. You redeemed them by Your great power and mighty hand.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel are Your servants.
They are also Your people.
You redeemed them.
You used Your great power to redeem them.
You used Your strong hand to redeem them.
passages.original: וְהֵ֥ם עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וְעַמֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּדִ֙יתָ֙ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ הַגָּד֔וֹל וּבְיָדְךָ֖ הַחֲזָקָֽה׃

passages.text: O Lord, may Your ear be attentive to my prayer and to the prayers of Your servants who delight to revere Your name. Give Your servant success this day, I pray, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” (At that time I was the cupbearer to the king.)
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the cupbearer to the king.
He prayed to the Lord.
He said, “O Lord, listen to my prayer.
Listen also to the prayers of Your servants.
These servants want to honor Your name.
Please give success to Your servant today.
Let this man show me mercy.”
passages.original: אָנָּ֣א אֲדֹנָ֗י תְּהִ֣י נָ֣א אָזְנְךָֽ־ קַ֠שֶּׁבֶת אֶל־ תְּפִלַּ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֜ וְאֶל־ תְּפִלַּ֣ת עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽחֲפֵצִים֙ לְיִרְאָ֣ה אֶת־ שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וְהַצְלִֽיחָה־ נָּ֤א לְעַבְדְּךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וּתְנֵ֣הוּ לְרַחֲמִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַאֲנִ֛י הָיִ֥יתִי מַשְׁקֶ֖ה לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
